title: Understanding Minimum Wage Rates Australia: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using minimum wage rates Australia. Includes National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equals $52,254.80 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are industry- or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and are often higher. Most employees under an award must be paid at least the award rate, which may include additional allowances or penalty rates.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour for casuals. When using the timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading – do not type a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay by your employer. For example, on a $26.44 hourly rate for 38 hours a week, super would be about $120.59 per week, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your current wage, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay is essential. The basic formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time employees, we assume a standard 38-hour week as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you a gross annual figure before tax and super.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year (gross).

If you are a casual worker, you add 25% loading, making the rate $33.05 per hour, which annualises to $65,318.80.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Commission defines the standard full-time week as 38 hours for the National Minimum Wage. Many awards also use this base. When you use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, we assume 38 hours unless you specify otherwise. Always check your award or agreement – some industries have different ordinary hours.

## Minimum Wage Rates Australia: National vs Award

When people search for **minimum wage rates australia**, they often find two key figures: the National Minimum Wage and award rates. The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours).

However, most Australian workers are covered by a modern award. Awards set higher minimum rates for specific industries and occupations. For example, a retail employee or a hospitality worker will have a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award. If you are unsure which applies to you, check your employment contract or visit the [pay guides](/blog) page.

**Important:** The National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a median. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026) – that is an average across all full-time employees, not a median for any specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and award.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), never type a rate that already includes casual loading – instead, use the checkbox to add it automatically. The loading compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave.

## Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (close to the official $1,004.90 due to rounding)
- Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

If you are paid weekly, your gross is $1,004.72. These figures help you budget and compare with salary offers.

## Tax and Superannuation

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies marginal tax rates for 2026–27:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here).

For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,254.80), tax would be approximately:
- Nil on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on $7,254.80 ($2,176.44)
- Total tax ≈ $6,196.44, plus Medicare $1,045.10, leaving about $45,013.26 take-home.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For the NMW worker, that adds about $6,270.58 per year to your super account. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an employer contribution. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/about) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Remember to check the casual loading box if applicable. The results include an estimate of tax and super, but note the disclaimer: this is not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability. Always consult a professional for your specific situation.

## Summary

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour; award rates are often higher.
- Casual loading adds 25% on top.
- Super is 12% paid on top, up to the limit.
- Tax is based on 2026–27 resident rates plus Medicare.

Understanding **minimum wage rates australia** helps you know your rights and compare job offers. Use our tools to convert your pay and plan your finances.
